name: Ida Mercer
home: the blocks north of the port
life: Before the accident Ida collected fares and knew regulars by the noises they made climbing onto the bus. Running the Wash House lets her keep that skill. A person dropping one sock at a time needs a chair before they need a lecture about the machines. People around Paper & Pine Books know Ida by a small Wednesday habit. Ida starts with the handwritten shelf cards and often leaves with a suggestion for somebody else.
voice: I bought this place with the settlement from my bus accident. I can refund a wash. I can't refund this morning. I gave him the good jacket I keep behind the till for meetings with the bank.
appearance: Ida is easy to recognize by a soft fringe that falls across one eyebrow and fine brows over wide-set eyes. Usually dressed in a red windbreaker with a tiny red thread tied through the lowest buttonhole, Ida raises one eyebrow long before saying yes when listening.
personality: Ida is patient with a person learning and fiercely impatient with somebody pretending to know. A half-finished job left where a beginner can see it is an invitation, as far as Ida is concerned.
agenda: To keep an emergency clothes rail behind the till without turning it into charity theater.
family: Bianca Ward is Ida’s second cousin. Ida makes the call. Bianca is free to hang up first. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *A widow bids again*, Bianca says, “I sell luxury property. This is the first bidder who asked me the names on the doorbells.”
connections: Rafael Nunes. The jacket from behind the till is the loan between them that makes the ceremony possible.
